answer.location_description: Small patch at the extreme top-right corner of the image: rows 0-3, columns about 21-23 (strongest at rows 0-2, columns 22-23). This is far from the centred nodule.
answer.mechanism: 1) Benign-leaning hidden units carry tightly localised negative weights on the top-right corner pixels. These are the high-bias nodule-template units 0, 2, 3, 5, 13, 15, 20, 24, 25, 27, 28 and 31: positive 3x3 core, negative ring, positive outer band. They mostly reach the output through layer-2 units u0, u7, u9 and u12, which have negative output weights. A bright corner therefore suppresses these units and lowers the benign evidence. 2) Several malignant-leaning units (6, 9 and 30, plus 12 and 16 weakly) have positive weights at the same pixels. Their layer-2 pathway runs mainly through u4, u13, u15 and u8, which have positive output weights, so they add malignant evidence. Both pathways push the logit toward class 1 when the corner is bright.
answer.evidence: Unit 27, rows 0-2, cols 22-23: (-33,-30), (-44,-20), (-35,-44). Unit 2, rows 0-3, cols 21-23: (-21,-21), (-14,-33), (-24,-22), (-26,-23). Unit 28: (-22,-26), (-6,-26), (-21,-19). Unit 15: (-19,-37), (-33,-21). Unit 20: (-19,-33), (-32,-17). Unit 3: (-28,-12), (-13,-23), (-11,-22). Unit 31: (-13,-22), (-6,-22), (4,-32). Units 13, 5 and 0 show similar values (-23 to -12). In all these units the immediately adjacent pixels at cols 18-21 are positive, so the corner is a sharp, separate feature rather than smooth lung texture. Malignant-direction units show the opposite sign at the same pixels: unit 9 (28,14), (23,13), (22,4), (18,26); unit 6 (10,30), (11,27); unit 30 (1,21), (2,19). Approximate summed pathway contributions are strongly negative for unit 0 (about -21,000 units) and strongly positive for units 6, 9, 10 and 16. Nodule anatomy should not have a fixed position in the image corner, which is why I read this as a shortcut. Caveat: units 19 and 23 have broad negative weights over the whole top-right strip (rows 0-2, cols 13-23), which partly counteracts this, so the direction is not fully clean.
answer.main_feature: The real feature is nodule size/extent at the image centre. Benign-leaning units are templates for a small bright core (rows 10-13, cols 10-13) surrounded by a darker ring (rows 7-9 and 14-16), i.e. a small well-circumscribed nodule. Malignant-leaning units (6, 9, 10, 12, 16, 30, and 19/23 more broadly) respond to bright tissue extending into that ring and beyond, i.e. larger or irregular nodules.
